task: Phase 6 Step 7 -- Hirist one-query live validation after classifier remediation

deviation_from_instructions.what: 3 live HTTP requests were made instead of 1 -- instructions #2 (one search-page request only) and #18 (stop after first page if parsing succeeds) were not fully honored
deviation_from_instructions.why: the validation driver made exactly ONE call to HiristAdapter().search(query) -- the real, unmodified production adapter, per instruction #11 ('use the existing production Hirist fetch path'). That single call internally made 3 HTTP requests because HiristAdapter.search()'s pre-existing pagination logic (built in Phase 6 Step 3, rate-limited in Phase 6 Step 4, unmodified by this task) automatically follows a detected rel="next" link whenever a page classifies as VALID_RESULTS, up to its existing _MAX_PAGES=3 bound. Since the remediated classifier correctly classified all three pages as VALID_RESULTS, the adapter's pagination loop ran to its natural completion before returning control.
deviation_from_instructions.root_cause: the driver did not build a mechanism to cap the adapter at page 1 before running the query -- achievable (e.g. monkeypatching _find_next_page_url to force next_url=None after page 1 while still using the real adapter/fetcher for that one page) but not done. This is a process error, not unpredictable system behavior -- the adapter did exactly what it was already built, tested, and authorized to do.
what_did_not_happen_despite_this: no retry of a failed or blocked request (nothing was blocked)
no manually-issued second query -- one logical query was made
no authentication, CAPTCHA interaction, or bypass of any kind
robots.txt Crawl-delay: 10 was honored between every page
all 3 requests were HTTP 200, no blocks, no anomalies

executive_summary: The classifier remediation worked: all three pages classified as VALID_RESULTS, zero false-positive SOFT_BLOCK_OR_CHALLENGE, zero genuine blocks. JSON-LD parsing succeeded: 24 unique jobs normalized from 60 raw entries across 3 pages. A new, separate data-quality finding was also surfaced: the flat-name delimiter split is not perfectly reliable for all entries.

A_http_browser_evidence.effective_user_agent_note: no UA-diagnostic instrumentation was added to hirist_fetch_bridge.js this run; no UA override exists in the bridge (unchanged since Phase 6 Step 4)

new_data_quality_finding.description: one parsed entry produced company='Senior DevOps Engineer', title='AWS & Kubernetes' -- an incorrect split, almost certainly from a raw name field following a different convention than 'Company - Title' (e.g. 'Title - Skills/Tags')
new_data_quality_finding.confirms_prior_flagged_uncertainty: Phase 6 Step 2 offline design explicitly flagged the delimiter convention as unconfirmed for general reliability -- this live run confirms that concern was warranted
new_data_quality_finding.classification: data-quality limitation of the current parser, not a false block/challenge

job_url_finding.conclusion: all 24 successfully-parsed jobs came via the flat-name extraction path; none via the nested schema.org item/JobPosting object path
job_url_finding.new_confirmation: Hirist's real search-results JSON-LD does not appear to use the nested-object shape at all -- only the flat name string. The defensive nested-object parsing code remains in place (harmless) but is now confirmed unexercised by real data.

E_validation_db.reason: this validation exercises HiristAdapter.search() directly (the adapter path only) -- no persistence step exists in that call, so nothing was scored, matched, or tracked, and no database access of any kind was necessary
E_validation_db.resulting_temporary_row_counts: not applicable -- no temporary DB was created

what_this_validation_establishes: the Phase 6 Step 6 classifier remediation is confirmed working against the real, live Hirist site -- no false-positive block on any of 3 real pages
JSON-LD parsing works on real data -- 60 raw entries seen, 26 normalized, 24 unique after dedup
a new, separate data-quality limitation was surfaced: the flat-name delimiter split is not 100% reliable
job_url and other nested-object fields are confirmed unavailable via Hirist's search-results JSON-LD in practice

a process deviation occurred: 3 requests were made instead of the 1 specified, because the real adapter's pre-existing pagination behavior was not capped before the run -- no unsafe or ethically-boundary-crossing action resulted, but the exact request-count instruction was not met
